Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space on June 16, 1963, aboard the Vostok 6 mission. A former textile worker and skydiver, Tereshkova completed 48 orbits around Earth in just under 71 hours. She remains the only woman to have flown a solo space mission. Mission Details: Launched at age 26, her flight lasted 70 hours and 50 minutes, orbiting the Earth 48 times. Selection: She was chosen from over 400 applicants due to her expertise in parachuting, as cosmonauts had to eject and parachute from their capsules upon return. Legacy: As detailed in her Wikipedia biography and Britannica entry, she became a major general in the Soviet Air Force and later a prominent politician. Wikipedia biography Britannica entry Background: The European Space Agency notes she was born in 1937 in central Russia and was selected for the cosmonaut corps in 1962.
